                                        Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently en-          plification leads to a form of temporal myopia. However,
                                        abled robotic manipulation by grounding visual and lin-        long-horizon manipulation requires reasoning that extends
                                        guistic cues into actions. However, most VLAs assume           beyond the present, maintaining temporal continuity across
                                        the Markov property, relying only on the current observa-      visual, language, and motor modalities. Without such tem-
                                        tion and thus suffering from temporal myopia that degrades     poral reasoning, dependencies between consecutive actions
                                        long-horizon coherence. In this work, we view motion as a      deteriorate, resulting in fragmented trajectories and dimin-
                                        more compact and informative representation of temporal        ished task-level coherence.
                                        context and world dynamics, capturing inter-state changes
                                        while filtering static pixel-level noise. From this perspec-       Recent efforts [26, 35, 54] have sought to alleviate this
                                        tive, HiF-VLA equips a motion-centric world model for the      temporal myopia by incorporating historical context, most
                                        VLA, enabling agents to reason about temporal dynam-           commonly by stacking multiple past observation frames.
                                        ics for future evolution during action generation. Build-      However, this approach is fundamentally limited. Stack-
                                        ing on this idea, we propose HiF-VLA (Hindsight, Insight,      ing raw frames is not only computationally prohibitive and
                                        and Foresight for VLAs), a unified framework that lever-       increases inference latency, hindering real-time control (see
                                        ages motion for bidirectional temporal reasoning. HiF-         Tab. 3), but it also introduces substantial pixel-level redun-
                                        VLA encodes past dynamics through hindsight priors, antic-     dancy. This deluge of static information often obscures the
                                        ipates future motion via foresight reasoning, and integrates   salient, task-relevant dynamics, making it difficult for the
                                        both through a hindsight-modulated joint expert to enable      model to distinguish meaningful changes from background
                                        a “think-while-acting” paradigm for long-horizon manip-        noise. We argue that a more precise and efficient represen-
                                        ulation. As a result, HiF-VLA surpasses strong baselines       tation of history is not the raw visual content of the past, but
                                        on LIBERO-Long and CALVIN ABC-D benchmarks, while              the motion that transpired between states. Motion serves as
                                        incurring negligible additional inference latency. Further-    a direct and compact proxy for temporal memory and en-
                                        more, HiF-VLA achieves substantial improvements in real-       vironment dynamics, faithfully capturing the dynamics of
                                        world long-horizon manipulation tasks, demonstrating its       interactions (such as an object being moved or a drawer be-
                                        broad effectiveness in practical robotic settings.             ing closed), while discarding redundant static information.

                                        56] have emerged as a promising framework for robotic

                                        els (VLMs) [1, 2, 10, 18, 34] to map visual and language

                                        representations to the action space. Despite progress, most

Temporal Modeling and Inference in Robotics. Tem-                                                                  Relying solely on instantaneous visual observations for ac-
poral modeling and foresight reasoning have been exten-                                                            tion decision-making often fails to provide stable percep-
sively studied in long video understanding and generation,                                                         tion, especially under challenging conditions such as occlu-
but remain relatively underexplored in robotic manipula-                                                           sion or repeated executions. Hence, capturing consistent
tion. Existing approaches largely focus on one-sided rea-                                                          dynamic patterns of the manipulator from historical states
soning. One line of work incorporates historical frames                                                            is critical. Existing approaches [8, 35, 37] typically main-
as visual prompts within the VLM input context, as in                                                              tain a sliding window of past observations and concatenate
TraceVLA [54], Octo [35], GR-2 [8], RoboVLMs [26]. An-                                                             them with the current observation to form a global repre-
other emphasizes foresight by predicting future visual sub-                                                        sentation. However, this frame-stacking strategy introduces
goals to guide action generation, such as CoT-VLA [52],                                                            significant redundancy: the high similarity between adja-
Seer [37], UniVLA [39], and UP-VLA [49], which typically                                                           cent frames makes it difficult for the model to focus on task-
condition an inverse dynamics model (IDM) on predicted                                                             relevant dynamics, potentially dispersing its attention.
future subgoals to infer actions. However, frame-level his-

torical encoding and pixel-level future prediction introduce

Figure 2. HiF-VLA Pipeline. (a) In Hindsight Prior Acquisition (see Sec. 3.2), HiF-VLA encodes dense historical frame sequences into
compact Motion Vector (MV) streams, forming structured hindsight primitives that capture temporal dynamics without pixel redundancy.
(b) In Foresight Reasoning with Insight (see Sec. 3.3), the VLM interprets the task instruction and current observation to infer plausible
foresight motions and corresponding latent action tokens. (c) Finally, the Hindsight-Modulated Joint Expert (see Sec. 3.4) fuses hindsight,
foresight, and action representations within a unified latent space, producing temporally consistent and causally coherent action predictions.

ding strategy of hindsight information affects model perfor-                    ference between pressed and unpressed states, making it
mance. Specifically, we compare two variants: (i) naı̈vely                      difficult for the baseline to detect successful actuation. In
concatenating hindsight with language and vision as direct                      contrast, HiF-VLA benefits from its broad temporal recep-
inputs to the VLM, and (ii) conditioning hindsight within                       tive field, enabling reliable detection of subtle state transi-
the expert module, which is adopted in our implementa-                          tions and robust execution of long-horizon tasks, resulting

consistently achieves higher success rates than VLM-based

hindsight may interfere with the pretrained alignment be-
tween visual and language representations. In contrast, in-                     This work introduces HiF-VLA, an efficient and unified
jecting hindsight at the decoding stage provides a more di-                     framework for temporal perception and reasoning built
rect, residual-like path for motion information. This allows                    upon low-dimensional, structured motion vectors. By
the low-level dynamics encoded in the hindsight to guide                        integrating hindsight, insight, and foresight cues, HiF-
future action prediction without passing through, and poten-                    VLA establishes a bidirectional temporal expansion over a
tially being corrupted by the VLM’s semantic fusion layers.                     sparse visual receptive field, enabling the robot to capture

approach in real-world applications, we conduct real-world                      demonstrates strong performance. Limitations. The cur-
experiments using the AgileX Piper robot. As shown in                           rent motion representation remains dependent on estima-
Fig. 5(a), a RealSense D435 camera captures the scene from                      tion accuracy and may be sensitive to noise in highly dy-
a third-view, while an additional USB camera is mounted                         namic scenes. We leave the exploration of large-scale pre-
on the robot’s wrist for egocentric observations. We col-                       training on internet videos to enhance motion understanding
lect three long-horizon tasks, each with 100 demonstrations                     and generation capabilities for future work.
involving diverse manipulation primitives, including pick,
place, stack, cover, and press.

6.1. Hindsight Encoder                                             AdaLN              AdaLN

We employ a 4-layer Vision Transformer (ViT) [11] as the                   Hindsight             Hindsight-Modulated Joint
hindsight motion encoder. The hindsight motion sequence                    Encoder                         Expert
of length h is first partitioned into (h//2) × (H//2) ×
(W//2) spatiotemporal blocks using a 3D convolution,
which simultaneously reduces temporal redundancy and            Figure 6. Architecture of the hindsight-modulated joint expert.
preserves local motion continuity. These blocks, together
with an additional [CLS] token that aggregates global tem-
poral context, are fed into the Transformer. The resulting
historical features are subsequently projected via a linear    7. Comparison with Video-Generation VLAs
layer into the joint expert embedding space, ensuring di-
mensional compatibility with the foresight and action path-
ways. This design allows the hindsight encoder to provide      Compared to VLA approaches that rely on video genera-
structured historical priors that can effectively regularize   tion [8, 13, 41, 43], our method differs fundamentally in
downstream decision-making.                                    how it models temporal dynamics. A large body of recent
